item.title: Daughters walked off with money
item.description:
Sarah Ort changed the account status so that she could take the money in the account.

Salomon Smith Barney letter confirming Sarah Ort’s custodial account was changed to an individual account (Dec. 1999)

Note: All this was being done December 1999, when R’ Avraham was still living at home, trying desperately to make the marriage work! R’ Avraham only became aware of this on the date of the letter, September 2002, three years later. That is why when the same daughter came to him saying that she “has no money” he gave her $2,500 in April 2000.

The next sister, Miriam Hirsch, followed suit.

The second daughter, Miriam (Ort) Hirsch, followed in her older sister’s footsteps. She was told to rely on the “secret hetter” and take possession of the money in her account. She did so.

item.title: Married daughters suing their father in court
item.description:
The two married daughters sued their father in secular courts without permission of beis din. The basis of the claim was his allegedly withholding part of the income from a piece of real estate he had put in their names.

When questioned by Rav Nota Greenblatt shlit”a, Av Beis Din of Memphis Tenn., what gave Mrs. Broderick the right to take her father to court, her husband, Raanan Broderick responded that they had a Heter from a Secret Rov, whose reason for the Heter was “also a secret.”

item.title: The Adler Story
item.description:
What happened, according to the documents

R’ Avraham Ort’s mother passed away in November 1999. In January 2000, Mrs. Manya Ort moved $350,000 out of her late mother-in-law’s account at Discount Bank and wired it to an Israel account of Mrs. Ort Sr. that already held $250,000. She then gave the combined $600,000 to her cousin R’ Ira (Yitzchak) Adler of Monsey, NY, with instructions to disburse it to “a yeshiva” — which yeshiva was never named.

item.title: Who Went to Court, and Who to Beis Din?
item.description:
The question

As posed in the correspondence: the impression from Mrs. Ort’s camp is that only after R’ Avrohom took her to secular court and lost is he now insisting on Beis Din — and since he accepted binding arbitration, why is he complaining? This page answers with documents.

Who filed first

Page 8 of the Final Arbitration Ruling, headed “Procedural History,” states that Mrs. Ort filed the divorce complaint on February 4, 2000, accompanied by an Order to Show Cause freezing assets — including the children’s and the Dove Foundation’s assets — and that a March 6, 2000 order continued the restraint: Page 8 of the Final Arbitration Ruling: procedural history of the divorce — view .
